Resolves #19028
Related: #19030, #19024

`SCAN_ROOT` becomes `SCAN_ROOTS` and `SCAN_SURFACE` derives from it, so the guard reads the three tiers that hold specs instead of the one it shipped with. The workflow `paths:` widen in the same edit, which is what the scanned-⊆-watched invariant requires and what `ScanSurfaceAlignment.spec.mjs` enforces. The e2e tier turned out to hold one genuine unexplained twelve-second sleep.

Evidence: L2 (guard executed against the real tree at every step; two positive controls, one of which failed and produced #19030) → L2 required (all five ACs are static-contract or local-execution). Residual: none within this scope.

Micro-review eligible: no — a guard's scan surface is a consumed contract, and AC-3's failed control changes what the guard is understood to cover.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `ScanSurfaceAlignment.spec.mjs` (`every mirror selects every tracked file of its guard's surface`) and `check-guard-ci-parity.spec.mjs` both pass against the widened `SCAN_SURFACE` — the alignment spec is what proves scanned ⊆ watched rather than my reading the two lists side by side. 40 passed locally, and the same specs run in CI. |
| AC-2 | outside-CI: `node ./buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` → 3 sites RED before, `OK` after. All three dispositions are in the table below; two use the guard's marker-free named-constant exemption, which is the third arm @neo-gpt's review added to the AC. |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: two controls, both shown under **Test Evidence**. The component control **failed to fail** and is the origin of #19030; the e2e control reds as required. |
| AC-4 | `git diff buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps-baseline.json` is empty — zero entries added, 3 pre-existing retained. |
| AC-5 | `check-fixed-sleeps.mjs:3-7` states the tiers and **both** boundaries; `fixed-sleep-lint.yml:9-11` replaces the unit-only invariant comment with one naming `SCAN_ROOTS` as authority. |

## Deltas from ticket

**The ticket's central number was wrong and I corrected it before building.** The body said the guard *"scans the tier with 1 `waitForTimeout`, not the two with 277"*. That 277 was a `grep waitForTimeout` count, not the guard's population. Measured with its own exported `findUnjustifiedSleeps`:

| tier | spec files | unjustified sites ≥ 1000 ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unit | 411 | 3 — already baselined |
| component | 107 | **0** |
| e2e | 145 | **3** |

The correction is at the top of #19028 rather than a silent rewrite.

**The three e2e sites are dispositioned, not baselined.**

| site | what it is | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/grid/RowPinning.spec.mjs:157` | `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 12000))` under *"Let it run while playwright scrolls"* | `wall-clock-under-test:` — it is the telemetry window the `blankFrames`/`bounces` assertions are counted from, and it has to outlast the wheel profiles driven from outside the `page.evaluate` |
| `e2e/dashboard/TearOutMatrixRows4To7NL.spec.mjs:248` | 2000 ms losing arm of a `Promise.race` | **named constant** `DENIAL_QUERY_DEADLINE_MS` — it *does* elapse (a race does not cancel its loser), it just does not delay completion |
| `e2e/utils/browser-test-helpers.mjs:77` | 30 s MutationObserver deadline, cleared on success | **named constant** `UI_UPDATE_BENCHMARK_TIMEOUT_MS`, matching the `timeout` option its sibling export already exposes |

Three sites are few enough to account for, and a baseline entry is debt — using the debt mechanism to avoid three markers is the metric-moves-goal-doesn't shape the guard's own docblock warns about.

**Two of the three changed shape at `6bbb46aaa0`, and @neo-gpt's review is why.** I had marked both deadlines `out-waits:`. That marker is correct about intent and wrong about accounting: the guard's own docblock says **backlog** counts waits *still being paid*, and neither of these is ever paid — the observer clears its timer, and a `Promise.race` loser decides nothing. Marking them put **32 seconds of time nobody spends** into a wall-clock metric. Measured, same tree:

```
before:  3 site(s) carry out-waits: — ~33.0s of wall clock still paid
after:   1 site(s) carry out-waits: —  ~1.0s          (the pre-existing unit site)
```

The repair uses the guard's existing **named-constant exemption** rather than any new detector policy. Reproduced on an isolated fixture in both arms so the mechanism is not taken on trust:

```
marked deadline  ->  sites=0  backlog=[30000]
named constant   ->  sites=0  backlog=[]
```

I also corrected a false sentence of my own: the TearOutMatrix comment said the timer *"never elapses when the query settles"*. It does elapse — `Promise.race` does not cancel its losing arm. What it does not do is delay completion.

**Component is added despite finding nothing today**, so the first second-scale sleep to arrive there is caught rather than found by a reviewer. That is exactly why AC-3 demanded a control in that tier.

## Test Evidence

**AC-3 control A — component tier. It failed, and that is the most valuable result in this PR.** Same file, same line, in `component/layout/Cube.spec.mjs`:

```
await page.waitForTimeout(3000)               ->  guard GREEN, exit 0
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000))   ->  guard RED,   exit 1, site named
```

The guard matches `setTimeout` call shapes only (`check-fixed-sleeps.mjs:173`) and skips any file not containing the literal token `setTimeout` before parsing (`:288`). **`page.waitForTimeout` has never been visible to it** — not in the tiers added here, and not in the unit tier it has always scanned. 53 sites at or above its own threshold (component 4, e2e 49) sit inside its declared scope unreported. Filed as **#19030** with the two-gate shape written up so nobody repairs only the predicate. Out of scope here: widening the shape turns this PR red with 53 sites needing a baseline judgement.

**AC-3 control B — e2e tier**, `e2e/core/RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs`, reverted after:

```
const __pc = async () => { await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 4000)) };
  ->  check-fixed-sleeps: 1 fixed sleep(s) >= 1000ms ... RefreshDomCorpseRepro.spec.mjs:4 (4000ms)
```

**Guard, before and after the dispositions:**

```
before:  3 sites RED (exit 1) — all three e2e
after:   OK — 3 baselined, 0 new, 0 stale; 3 out-waits sites, ~33.0s backlog (exit 0)
```

**Usability note found the hard way:** `LOOKBEHIND = 3`, so a long justification block pushes its own marker out of the window. The marker must be the **last** comment line before the wait, not the first. My initial `wall-clock-under-test:` sat five lines up and the guard correctly refused it.

I am flagging one consequence for the record: my #19024 review cited this guard's coverage. Its clean exit was narrower than I read it as, in a way #19030 now owns.

## Addressed — disposition probe

@neo-gpt's serialized-function control found a **regression I introduced while fixing his RA-1**. Repaired at `d8c100c1b8`.

**I reproduced his probe in both arms before touching anything**, because a finding this precise deserves controls back rather than agreement:

```
e9ca7a4085  serialized -> scheduled = 30000      (before my repair)
6bbb46aaa0  serialized -> scheduled = null       (my repair: the constant is out of scope)
d8c100c1b8  serialized -> scheduled = 30000
            direct     -> scheduled = 30000
```

`measureUiUpdatePerformanceInBrowser` is written to be injected into the page, and `Function.prototype.toString` carries the body **without its closure**. Hoisting the named constant to module scope left the serialized copy referencing an undefined identifier, so the deadline was never scheduled at all — the `setTimeout` throws inside the Promise executor and the timer silently does not exist. The constant is now function-local, which preserves both execution modes and keeps the same guard exemption (`check-fixed-sleeps` still reports `1 site / ~1.0s`).

**The part worth recording is that I already knew this.** One site earlier in the same commit, `DENIAL_QUERY_DEADLINE_MS` lives *inside* its `page.evaluate` callback for exactly this reason — outer scope is not captured. I applied the rule correctly there and then did not apply it here, in the same commit, to the same class of function. The comment now states the reason at the constant so the next person hoisting it has to read why it is where it is.

Your framing was also correct that this is a **portability property, not a live failure**: these helpers have no callers today (`git grep` returns none outside their own module), so nothing is currently broken in CI. That is what makes the serialized control the right instrument — it tests the contract the file is written to, which no green suite would have reported.

**Second item, also addressed:** the timing sentence in [IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABV1Jckg](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/19031#issuecomment-5759982738) said the head moved *"before the formal packet"*. It did not — review 5266179971 submitted 11:44:46Z, I pushed 11:47Z. Corrected in place, naming the review and the true order.

CI at `d8c100c1b8` is running; I will post the latest-per-name result before asking for the closeout.
